question: When caring for patients, why do we look at 'basic human needs' instead of just treating their illness?

options.A: To minimize the need for doctor prescriptions
options.C: Understanding the whole person beyond just the disease
options.D: To speed up the patient discharge process

explanation: You've got this! Looking at basic needs reminds us we are caring for a complete human being, not just a medical chart or a diagnosis. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do patients often struggle to meet their own basic needs when they get sick and come to the hospital?

options.A: Hospitals strictly forbid patients from eating or drinking
options.B: Family members are always present to take over every task
options.C: Patients completely forget their personal habits during sickness
options.D: Illness and hospitalization disrupt a person's normal independence

explanation: Spot on! Sickness and unfamiliar hospital routines can make it hard for patients to do things they normally handle easily on their own. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which level of Maslow's hierarchy sits at the very bottom of the pyramid?
explanation: Physiological needs form the base of the pyramid because they are essential for immediate human survival. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h2)

question: A mom in labor is in severe pain from strong contractions and crying out. What should you, as her midwife, address first?

options.A: Her self-esteem regarding her ability to mother
options.B: Her desire for community and social interaction
options.C: Her immediate physiological pain and comfort
options.D: Her need for self-actualization and personal growth

explanation: Exactly! When a patient is in acute physical distress, immediate pain relief and comfort always come first before we focus on other needs. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is considered a primary physiological survival need?
explanation: Oxygen is a fundamental biological requirement without which a person cannot survive for more than a few minutes. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why do midwives keep a close eye on a mother's urine output during a long, hard labor?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the unborn baby
options.B: To test for blood group compatibility
options.C: To evaluate hydration status and kidney function
options.D: To determine when the placenta will separate

explanation: Great job! Tracking urine helps you know if the mother is staying well-hydrated and how her kidneys are coping with the physical stress of labor. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which simple action is a great way to create physical safety for your patients on the ward?

options.A: Sharing patient medical records with curious visitors
options.B: Practicing proper hand hygiene before touching patients
options.C: Leaving wet floor spills uncleaned in the hallway
options.D: Administering drugs without checking the patient ID band

explanation: You nailed it! Hand hygiene stops the spread of nasty germs and keeps your patients physically safe from hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does making a patient feel emotionally safe and secure help their physical body recover?

options.A: It eliminates the requirement for nutritional support
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never experience pain
options.C: It lowers patient anxiety, which helps stabilize vital signs
options.D: It replaces the need for any surgical intervention

explanation: Makes total sense! When a patient feels mentally at ease, their stress drops, leading to calmer heart rates and steadier blood pressure. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a practical way you can support a new mother's need for love and belonging right after birth?

options.A: Discouraging visitors from entering the maternity ward
options.B: Limiting conversation to strict medical charts only
options.C: Encouraging early skin-to-skin contact with her newborn
options.D: Isolating her completely from all family members

explanation: Wonderful! Skin-to-skin sparks that instant emotional bond and secure attachment between the new mother and her baby. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is welcoming family members to stay with hospitalized patients so important in Nigerian healthcare?

options.A: It aligns with cultural values of communal support and reduces patient anxiety
options.B: It ensures that family members pay all medical bills on time
options.C: It removes the legal liability of the hospital entirely
options.D: It allows hospital staff to completely stop monitoring the patient

explanation: Spot on! Community and family are huge parts of our culture. Having loved ones close brings deep emotional comfort when someone is unwell. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which action actively protects a patient's self-esteem and personal dignity?

options.A: Discussing the patient's private diagnosis loudly in the hallway
options.B: Ignoring the patient's preferences regarding daily hygiene
options.C: Drawing privacy curtains and asking permission before an exam
options.D: Making decisions for the patient without consulting them

explanation: You got this! Respecting their private space and asking for consent lets patients know they are valued human beings, not just cases. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h6)

question: What usually happens to a patient psychologically when their dignity and self-esteem are constantly brushed aside?

options.A: Immediate physical failure of the cardiovascular system
options.B: Permanent physical impairment of the musculoskeletal limbs
options.C: Feelings of helplessness, loss of control, and lowered morale
options.D: Sudden development of contagious infectious diseases

explanation: That's right. When we ignore a person's dignity, they feel defeated and lose their sense of control, which hurts their emotional healing. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h6)

question: What represents the highest level of Maslow's human needs hierarchy?
explanation: Self-actualization sits at the top of the pyramid as the ultimate goal of personal growth and fulfillment. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h7)

question: A patient recovering well from surgery starts asking how to change her lifestyle to prevent future illness and help others in her community. Which need level does this show?
explanation: Brilliant! When someone looks past just getting better to personal growth and helping others, they are operating at the self-actualization level. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h7)

question: When planning patient care, which type of problem must always be tackled first?
explanation: You've got it! Keeping the patient alive and safe from harm always takes top priority over social or emotional wants. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is it a mistake to view human needs as strict, separate boxes that never overlap?

options.A: Physiological needs are completely unimportant during acute illness
options.B: Patients only ever experience one need at a single point in time
options.C: Psychosocial support always replaces the need for medications
options.D: Different need levels often overlap and influence each other simultaneously

explanation: Spot on! Human life is messy and connected. For example, easing a patient's physical pain often requires giving them emotional reassurance at the exact same time. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h8)
